defmodule ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Engine.GraphEngineServer do
  @moduledoc """
  The GraphEngineServer is the central cognitive hub for the ProCoder DAG Orchestrator.
  It maintains the state of the execution plan, processes atomic graph mutations,
  and orchestrates task lifecycles through topological validation and persistence.
  """

  use GenServer
  require Logger

  alias ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Types
  alias ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Types.GraphState
  alias ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Validation.GraphValidator
  alias ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Persistence.PersistenceEngine
  alias ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Recovery.RecoveryManager
  alias ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Lifecycle.TaskState

  @type t :: pid()

  # --- Client API ---

  @doc "Starts the GraphEngineServer."
  def start_link(opts) do
    session_id = Keyword.fetch!(opts, :session_id)
    GenServer.start_link(__MODULE__, session_id, name: via_tuple(session_id))
  end

  @doc "Registers a new node in the DAG."
  @spec add_node(pid() | String.t(), map()) :: :ok | {:error, term()}
  def add_node(engine_ref, attrs) do
    GenServer.call(engine_ref, {:add_node, attrs})
  end

  @doc "Registers a dependency edge between nodes."
  @spec add_edge(pid() | String.t(), String.t(), String.t()) :: :ok | {:error, term()}
  def add_edge(engine_ref, from_id, to_id) do
    GenServer.call(engine_ref, {:add_edge, from_id, to_id})
  end

  # --- GenServer Callbacks ---

  @impl true
  def init(session_id) do
    state = Types.new_state(session_id)
    {:ok, state}
  end

  @impl true
  def handle_call({:add_node, attrs}, _from, state) do
    with {:ok, node} <- Types.from_map(attrs),
         true <- !Map.has_key?(state.node_registry, node.id) do
      
      new_registry = Map.put(state.node_registry, node.id, node)
      new_graph = Graph.add_vertex(state.graph, node.id)

      case GraphValidator.validate_all!(new_graph, new_registry) do
        :ok ->
          PersistenceEngine.take_snapshot(self(), new_graph)
          :telemetry.execute([:procoder, :planner, :engine, :node_added], %{id: node.id})
          {:reply, :ok, %{state | node_registry: new_registry, graph: new_graph}}
        {:error, reason, _} ->
          {:reply, {:error, reason}, state}
      end
    else
      {:error, reason} -> {:reply, {:error, reason}, state}
      false -> {:reply, {:error, :node_already_exists}, state}
    end
  end

  @impl true
  def handle_call({:add_edge, from_id, to_id}, _from, state) do
    if Map.has_key?(state.node_registry, from_id) and Map.has_key?(state.node_registry, to_id) do
      new_graph = Graph.add_edge(state.graph, from_id, to_id)
      
      case GraphValidator.validate_all!(new_graph, state.node_registry) do
        :ok ->
          PersistenceEngine.take_snapshot(self(), new_graph)
          :telemetry.execute([:procoder, :planner, :engine, :edge_added], %{from: from_id, to: to_id})
          {:reply, :ok, %{state | graph: new_graph}}
        {:error, reason, _} ->
          {:reply, {:error, reason}, state}
      end
    else
      {:reply, {:error, :invalid_node_reference}, state}
    end
  end

  @impl true
  def handle_info({:task_failed, node_id, reason}, state) do
    Logger.error("Node #{node_id} failed: #{inspect(reason)}. Initiating recovery.")
    
    # Trigger recovery via RecoveryManager
    RecoveryManager.remediate(node_id, reason)
    
    # Update node state internally
    new_registry = Map.update!(state.node_registry, node_id, fn node ->
      {:ok, updated} = TaskState.transition(node, :failed)
      updated
    end)
    
    {:noreply, %{state | node_registry: new_registry}}
  end

  # --- Internal Helpers ---

  defp via_tuple(session_id), do: {:via, Registry, {ProCoder.Registry, "engine_#{session_id}"}}
end

defmodule ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Engine.DAGManager.Tests.DAGManagerConcurrencyRecoveryTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Integration test suite for the ProCoder DAG Orchestrator focusing on high-concurrency 
  scheduling, failure remediation, and persistent state integrity.
  """

  use ExUnit.Case, async: false

  alias ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Engine.GraphEngineServer
  alias ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Engine.DAGManager.DispatchLogic.DispatchCoordinator
  alias ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Engine.DAGManager.RecoveryLogic.FailureRemediator
  alias ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Persistence.PersistenceEngine
  alias ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Validation.GraphValidator
  alias ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Types

  @session_id "test_session_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"

  setup do
    # Provisioning the supervision tree for the DAG Manager
    {:ok, supervisor_pid} = ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Engine.DAGManager.Supervision.DAGOrchestratorSupervisor.start_link(@session_id)
    
    on_exit(fn ->
      if Process.alive?(supervisor_pid), do: Process.exit(supervisor_pid, :shutdown)
    end)

    {:ok, session_id: @session_id}
  end

  describe "High-Concurrency Stress Testing" do
    test "maintains graph integrity under rapid concurrent task completion" do
      engine_ref = via_tuple("engine", @session_id)
      
      # Setup: Inject 50 nodes with linear dependency
      for i <- 1..50 do
        GraphEngineServer.add_node(engine_ref, %{id: "task_#{i}", task_type: :compute})
        if i > 1 do
          GraphEngineServer.add_edge(engine_ref, "task_#{i-1}", "task_#{i}")
        end
      end

      # Spawn concurrent completions
      tasks = Enum.map(1..50, fn i ->
        Task.async(fn ->
          send(via_tuple("coordinator", @session_id), {:task_completed, "task_#{i}"})
        end)
      end)
      
      Enum.each(tasks, &Task.await/1)

      {graph, _registry} = GenServer.call(engine_ref, :get_state)
      assert Graph.vertices(graph) |> length() == 50
      assert Graph.is_acyclic?(graph)
    end
  end

  describe "Failure Remediation Fidelity" do
    test "triggers recovery on single-node failure and maintains acyclicity" do
      engine_ref = via_tuple("engine", @session_id)
      coordinator_ref = via_tuple("coordinator", @session_id)
      
      GraphEngineServer.add_node(engine_ref, %{id: "node_A", task_type: :compute})
      GraphEngineServer.add_node(engine_ref, %{id: "node_B", task_type: :compute})
      GraphEngineServer.add_edge(engine_ref, "node_A", "node_B")

      # Fail node A
      send(coordinator_ref, {:task_failed, "node_A", :io_error})
      
      # Wait for async remediation
      Process.sleep(200)

      {graph, _registry} = GenServer.call(engine_ref, :get_state)
      assert Graph.is_acyclic?(graph)
      assert Graph.has_vertex?(graph, "node_A")
    end

    test "cascading failure blocks children and triggers remediation" do
      engine_ref = via_tuple("engine", @session_id)
      coordinator_ref = via_tuple("coordinator", @session_id)
      
      GraphEngineServer.add_node(engine_ref, %{id: "parent", task_type: :compute})
      GraphEngineServer.add_node(engine_ref, %{id: "child1", task_type: :compute})
      GraphEngineServer.add_node(engine_ref, %{id: "child2", task_type: :compute})
      GraphEngineServer.add_edge(engine_ref, "parent", "child1")
      GraphEngineServer.add_edge(engine_ref, "parent", "child2")

      # Fail parent
      send(coordinator_ref, {:task_failed, "parent", :logic_failure})
      
      Process.sleep(300)

      {graph, _registry} = GenServer.call(engine_ref, :get_state)
      assert GraphValidator.contains_cycle?(graph) == false
    end
  end

  describe "Persistent State Integrity" do
    test "ensures snapshot captures remediated state" do
      engine_ref = via_tuple("engine", @session_id)
      persistence_ref = via_tuple("persistence", @session_id)
      coordinator_ref = via_tuple("coordinator", @session_id)

      GraphEngineServer.add_node(engine_ref, %{id: "critical_node", task_type: :compute})
      
      # Trigger failure which should trigger remediation -> snapshot
      send(coordinator_ref, {:task_failed, "critical_node", :io_error})
      
      Process.sleep(500)
      
      # Assert PersistenceEngine has history
      # Since we don't have direct access to internal state, we check if telemetry fired
      assert_receive {_, [:procoder, :planner, :persistence, :snapshot_taken], _, _}, 1000
    end
  end

  # Helpers
  defp via_tuple(type, session_id) do
    {:via, Registry, {ProCoder.Registry, "#{type}_#{session_id}"}}
  end
end

defmodule ProCoder.Planner.DAG.Manager.Requirements do
  @moduledoc """
  The authoritative, immutable source of truth for the DAG orchestration engine's
  environmental and dependency configuration.

  This module enforces system-wide constraints, validates runtime dependencies,
  and provides a secure integrity check mechanism for the ProCoder Planner.
  """

  require Logger

  @type version_spec :: String.t()
  @type dep_map :: %{atom() => version_spec()}
  @type spec_map :: %{
    dependencies: dep_map(),
    compatibility_matrix: map(),
    checksum: String.t()
  }

  @doc """
  Returns the immutable dependency specification manifest.
  """
  @spec get_spec() :: spec_map()
  def get_spec do
    %{
      dependencies: %{
        libgraph: "~> 0.16.0",
        jason: "~> 1.4.0"
      },
      compatibility_matrix: %{
        "elixir_1.15" => ["libgraph_0.16", "jason_1.4"],
        "elixir_1.16" => ["libgraph_0.16", "jason_1.4"]
      },
      # SHA-256 of the dependency map definition
      checksum: "7a22ba2eaae8411e497891a90f4f511b1301786d34a6dcde5a347adc01d68517"
    }
  end

  @doc """
  Acts as a gatekeeper for application startup. Performs recursive validation
  of the environment and dependency integrity. Fails fast if anomalies are detected.
  """
  @spec init!() :: :ok | no_return()
  def init! do
    spec = get_spec()

    # 1. Integrity Check (Fail-Fast)
    unless verify_checksum(spec) do
      Logger.emergency("Security Violation: DAG requirement manifest tampered.")
      raise "Security Violation: Dependency manifest checksum mismatch."
    end

    # 2. Dependency Loading Check
    Enum.each(spec.dependencies, fn {dep, _version} ->
      unless Code.ensure_loaded?(dep) do
        Logger.error("Environment Mismatch: Required dependency '#{dep}' not loaded.")
        raise "Environment Mismatch: Required dependency '#{dep}' not loaded."
      end
    end)

    :telemetry.execute([:procoder, :planner, :dag_requirements, :initialized], %{})
    :ok
  end

  @doc """
  Public health check interface for the supervisor tree to assess operational readiness.
  """
  @spec health_check() :: :ok | {:error, String.t()}
  def health_check do
    try do
      init!()
    rescue
      e ->
        {:error, Exception.message(e)}
    end
  end

  # --- Private Helpers ---

  defp verify_checksum(spec) do
    # Verify manifest integrity excluding the checksum field itself
    manifest_data = Map.delete(spec, :checksum)
    calculated =
      :crypto.hash(:sha256, :erlang.term_to_binary(manifest_data))
      |> Base.encode16(case: :lower)

    calculated == spec.checksum
  end
end

# ProCoder DAG Manager: Architectural and Technical Specification

## 1. Executive Summary
The DAG Manager subsystem constitutes the core planning intelligence for the ProCoder autonomous system. It manages the lifecycle of complex task plans by orchestrating state transitions within a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) structure. This document provides a exhaustive technical reference for its architecture, concurrent execution models, and self-healing mechanisms.

## 2. Core Architectural Philosophy
The DAG Manager is predicated on three foundational pillars:
- **Atomicity**: Every mutation to the planning graph must be atomic.
- **Cognitive Persistence**: The planning state is durably persisted, allowing for historical reconstruction (/rewind) and session continuity.
- **Fault-Tolerance**: The manager must be self-healing, utilizing automated remediation subgraphs when task nodes transition to :failed status.

## 3. High-Performance Concurrency Model
To meet the requirement of managing millions of nodes, the DAG Manager leverages the BEAM VM's strengths:
- **GenServer State Isolation**: Each planning session is encapsulated within its own GenServer process, preventing global state contention.
- **libgraph Integration**: Structural modeling relies on the `libgraph` library for efficient graph representation and topological sorting.
- **Asynchronous Actuation**: While planning and graph traversal occur within the DAG orchestrator, actual execution is delegated to the SessionManager via an asynchronous, non-blocking queue. This ensures that heavy IO operations or task execution do not stall the orchestration engine.
- **ETS-Backed Metadata**: Rapid access to node statuses (pending, running, completed, failed) is optimized through ETS tables, reducing read-locks on the primary graph structure.

## 4. Graph Orchestration Engine
The orchestrator operates as a lifecycle manager for task nodes.
### 4.1 State Machine Dynamics
The system follows a strict state transition model (Pending -> Running -> Completed/Failed). The GenServer maintains the mapping between internal node representations and the `libgraph` nodes.
### 4.2 Topological Dispatch Sequencer
The Dispatch Coordinator periodically performs `libgraph.topsort/1` to determine the set of 'ready' nodes (those with an in-degree of 0 among pending tasks). Rate-limiting logic is applied here to prevent overwhelming the SessionManager with task bursts.

## 5. Resilience and Self-Healing
### 5.1 Failure Remediator
When a node transitions to `:failed`, the Recovery Manager executes:
1. **Subgraph Pruning**: Identifies all downstream descendants reachable from the failed node and marks them for cancellation.
2. **Dynamic Remediation**: Uses node metadata to choose a compensation strategy (e.g., :retry, :rollback, :branch_prune).
3. **Graph Injection**: Generates and links a new remediation subgraph to the existing DAG, ensuring the execution flow remains structurally valid.

## 6. Persistence and Audit Trail
### 6.1 Two-Tiered Storage
- **Hot Stack (Memory)**: Maintains recent DAG snapshots for rapid /rewind access.
- **Cold Stack (Repo/SQLite)**: Durable binary snapshots of the graph state serialized via `:erlang.term_to_binary`.
### 6.2 Integrity Verification
Every persistence event is checked via a SHA-256 hash. During recovery, the PersistenceEngine verifies the hash against the persisted state before rehydration to prevent malformed graph states from being loaded into memory.

## 7. Security and Integrity Guardrails
### 7.1 GraphValidator
Before any mutation, the GraphValidator enforces:
- **Acyclicity**: Prevention of circular dependencies.
- **Referential Integrity**: All edges must point to existing nodes within the registry.
- **Reachability**: Ensuring no orphan nodes exist that would be unreachable by the orchestrator.
### 7.2 Input Sanitization
The orchestrator treats all external inputs as untrusted. Payloads are validated against a predefined schema (TaskNode) before registration.

## 8. Scalability Strategy
The system is built for massive scaling:
- **Horizontal Session Scaling**: By session-isolating the DAGs, the orchestrator can scale horizontally across multiple BEAM nodes or system cores.
- **NIF-based Compute**: Compute-intensive graph algorithms are offloaded to Rustler NIFs, ensuring the BEAM scheduler is never starved.

## 9. Observability and Telemetry
Every internal transition, dispatch, failure, and recovery is logged to the `:telemetry` bus. This allows for real-time visualization of the planning process and historical analysis of task failures.

## 10. Operational Procedures
- **Rewinding**: Invoking `/rewind <timestamp>` reconstructs the `libgraph` object by querying the persistence layer for the closest available snapshot and re-running any intermediate graph mutations, if necessary.
- **Manual Intervention**: The state machine allows for human-in-the-loop overrides, which are treated as high-priority 'remediation tasks' injected into the DAG.

## 11. Implementation Guidelines
- All graph operations must be contained within the GenServer process.
- Strictly avoid blocking IO calls in any core orchestrator process.
- Use `dialyzer` to enforce type safety on graph mutations.

## 12. Conclusion
The DAG Manager subsystem provides the robust, fault-tolerant, and high-performance backbone for ProCoder's planning engine. By combining structural rigor (libgraph), durable storage (SQLite), and aggressive self-healing, the manager ensures that the agent's goals remain achievable, even under extreme runtime conditions.

defmodule ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Engine.DAGManager.Supervision.DAGOrchestratorSupervisor do
  @moduledoc """
  The apex supervisor for a single DAG orchestrator planning session.

  Manages the lifecycle of:
  1. PersistenceEngine (Durability)
  2. GraphEngineServer (DAGEngine / State)
  3. DispatchCoordinator (Scheduler)
  4. FailureRemediator (RecoveryManager)

  Enforces ordered startup and granular fault isolation using a :one_for_one strategy.
  """

  use Supervisor
  require Logger

  alias ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Engine.GraphEngineServer
  alias ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Persistence.PersistenceEngine
  alias ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Engine.DAGManager.DispatchLogic.DispatchCoordinator
  alias ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Engine.DAGManager.RecoveryLogic.FailureRemediator
  alias ProCoder.Planner.DAG.Manager.Requirements

  @doc """
  Starts the DAGOrchestratorSupervisor for a specific session.
  """
  def start_link(session_id) when is_binary(session_id) do
    Supervisor.start_link(__MODULE__, session_id, name: via_tuple(session_id))
  end

  @impl true
  def init(session_id) do
    # Pre-flight environment check
    case Requirements.init!() do
      :ok ->
        children = [
          # Persistence must be live first to re-hydrate state
          {PersistenceEngine, [session_id: session_id]},
          # Graph Engine holds the primary DAG state
          {GraphEngineServer, [session_id: session_id]},
          # Coordinator schedules tasks based on graph state
          {DispatchCoordinator, [session_id: session_id]},
          # Remediation manager triggers compensation subgraphs on failure
          {FailureRemediator, [session_id: session_id]}
        ]

        # :one_for_one ensures isolation: one component crash does not cascade.
        # Max restart intensity: 10 restarts / 60 seconds (as per blueprint).
        Supervisor.init(children,
          strategy: :one_for_one,
          max_restarts: 10,
          max_seconds: 60
        )

      _ ->
        Logger.emergency("DAGOrchestratorSupervisor failed to start due to environment mismatch.")
        :ignore
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Telemetry wrapper for child process termination monitoring.
  """
  def handle_child_termination(session_id, child_module, reason) do
    :telemetry.execute(
      [:procoder, :planner, :supervisor, :child_terminated],
      %{reason: inspect(reason)},
      %{session_id: session_id, module: child_module}
    )
  end

  defp via_tuple(session_id), do: {:via, Registry, {ProCoder.Registry, "supervisor_#{session_id}"}}
end

defmodule ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Engine.DAGManager.DispatchLogic.DispatchCoordinator do
  @moduledoc """
  The Topological Dispatch Sequencer (TDS) is responsible for the orchestration
  of task execution within the ProCoder DAG Orchestrator.

  It interfaces with libgraph for topological sorting, maintains a ready-queue
  of dispatchable nodes, enforces rate-limiting, and manages task lifecycles
  via the SessionManager.
  """

  use GenServer
  require Logger

  alias ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Recovery.RecoveryManager
  alias ProCoder.SessionManager
  alias ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Types

  @type state :: %{
    session_id: String.t(),
    active_tasks: map(),
    max_concurrency: pos_integer()
  }

  @doc """
  Starts the DispatchCoordinator.
  """
  def start_link(opts) do
    session_id = Keyword.fetch!(opts, :session_id)
    GenServer.start_link(__MODULE__, session_id, name: via_tuple(session_id))
  end

  @doc """
  Triggers a dispatch cycle to evaluate the DAG and start eligible tasks.
  """
  @spec trigger_dispatch(pid() | String.t()) :: :ok
  def trigger_dispatch(coordinator_ref) do
    GenServer.cast(coordinator_ref, :dispatch_cycle)
  end

  # --- GenServer Callbacks ---

  @impl true
  def init(session_id) do
    {:ok, %{
      session_id: session_id,
      active_tasks: %{},
      max_concurrency: 10
    }}
  end

  @impl true
  def handle_cast(:dispatch_cycle, state) do
    try do
      engine_ref = get_engine_ref(state.session_id)
      # Assuming GraphEngineServer exposes :get_state returning {graph, registry}
      {graph, node_registry} = GenServer.call(engine_ref, :get_state)

      ready_nodes = find_ready_nodes(graph, node_registry)
      new_state = process_dispatch_queue(ready_nodes, state)

      {:noreply, new_state}
    rescue
      e ->
        Logger.error("Dispatch cycle failed: #{Exception.message(e)}")
        {:noreply, state}
    end
  end

  @impl true
  def handle_info({:task_completed, node_id}, state) do
    Logger.info("Node #{node_id} completed.")
    update_node_status(state.session_id, node_id, :completed)
    
    # Trigger new dispatch cycle
    trigger_dispatch(self())
    
    {:noreply, %{state | active_tasks: Map.delete(state.active_tasks, node_id)}}
  end

  @impl true
  def handle_info({:task_failed, node_id, reason}, state) do
    Logger.error("Node #{node_id} failed: #{inspect(reason)}")
    update_node_status(state.session_id, node_id, :failed)
    
    engine_ref = get_engine_ref(state.session_id)
    {graph, registry} = GenServer.call(engine_ref, :get_state)
    
    # Trigger Recovery Manager
    RecoveryManager.remediate(get_remediator_ref(state.session_id), node_id, reason, graph, registry)
    
    {:noreply, %{state | active_tasks: Map.delete(state.active_tasks, node_id)}}
  end

  # --- Internal Helpers ---

  defp find_ready_nodes(graph, registry) do
    # Filter nodes with 0 in-degree and status :pending
    graph
    |> Graph.topsort()
    |> Enum.filter(fn node_id ->
      node = Map.get(registry, node_id)
      node && node.status == :pending && Graph.in_degree(graph, node_id) == 0
    end)
  end

  defp process_dispatch_queue(nodes, state) do
    Enum.reduce_while(nodes, state, fn node_id, acc ->
      if map_size(acc.active_tasks) < acc.max_concurrency do
        dispatch_task(node_id, acc.session_id)
        {:cont, %{acc | active_tasks: Map.put(acc.active_tasks, node_id, :running)}}
      else
        {:halt, acc}
      end
    end)
  end

  defp dispatch_task(node_id, session_id) do
    SessionManager.actuate(session_id, node_id)
    :telemetry.execute([:procoder, :planner, :dispatch, :node], %{node_id: node_id})
  end

  defp update_node_status(session_id, node_id, status) do
    engine_ref = get_engine_ref(session_id)
    GenServer.cast(engine_ref, {:update_node_status, node_id, status})
  end

  defp get_engine_ref(session_id), do: {:via, Registry, {ProCoder.Registry, "engine_#{session_id}"}}
  defp get_remediator_ref(session_id), do: {:via, Registry, {ProCoder.Registry, "remediator_#{session_id}"}}
  defp via_tuple(session_id), do: {:via, Registry, {ProCoder.Registry, "dispatch_#{session_id}"}}
end

defmodule ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Engine.DAGManager.RecoveryLogic.FailureRemediator do
  @moduledoc """
  The FailureRemediator module handles autonomous self-healing for the ProCoder DAG Orchestrator.
  It intercepts task failures, performs recursive subgraph traversal to identify impacted nodes,
  and dynamically generates and validates compensation subgraphs to restore system integrity.
  """

  use GenServer
  require Logger

  alias ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Types.TaskNode
  alias ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Validation.GraphValidator
  alias ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Persistence.PersistenceEngine

  @type remediation_strategy :: :retry | :cleanup | :rerun | :branch_prune | :diagnostic_only

  @doc """
  Starts the FailureRemediator.
  """
  def start_link(opts) do
    GenServer.start_link(__MODULE__, opts, name: via_tuple(opts[:session_id]))
  end

  @doc """
  Triggers a remediation sequence for a failing node.
  Offloads the graph traversal and compensation generation to a task.
  """
  @spec remediate(pid() | String.t(), String.t(), atom(), Graph.t(), map()) :: :ok
  def remediate(remediator_ref, node_id, reason, graph, node_registry) do
    GenServer.cast(remediator_ref, {:remediate, node_id, reason, graph, node_registry})
  end

  # --- GenServer Callbacks ---

  @impl true
  def init(_opts) do
    {:ok, %{active_remediations: %{}}}
  end

  @impl true
  def handle_cast({:remediate, node_id, reason, graph, node_registry}, state) do
    Task.start(fn ->
      perform_remediation_workflow(node_id, reason, graph, node_registry)
    end)
    {:noreply, state}
  end

  # --- Internal Logic ---

  defp perform_remediation_workflow(node_id, reason, graph, node_registry) do
    try do
      # 1. Identify impacted subgraph
      impacted_nodes = identify_impacted_subgraph(graph, node_id)

      # 2. Map failure type to compensation strategy
      strategies = select_strategies(reason)

      # 3. Generate Compensation Subgraph
      compensation_dag = generate_compensation_subgraph(node_id, strategies, impacted_nodes)

      # 4. Topological Integrity Check
      case GraphValidator.validate_all!(compensation_dag, node_registry) do
        :ok ->
          # 5. Checkpoint & Actuate
          PersistenceEngine.take_snapshot(self(), compensation_dag)
          Logger.info("Remediation successful for #{node_id}: #{reason}")

        {:error, reason, _} ->
          Logger.error("Compensation DAG validation failed for #{node_id}: #{reason}")
          trigger_escalation(node_id, reason)
      end
    rescue
      e ->
        Logger.error("Critical failure in remediation workflow: #{Exception.message(e)}")
        trigger_escalation(node_id, :remediation_logic_failure)
    end
  end

  defp identify_impacted_subgraph(graph, failed_node_id) do
    # All nodes reachable from the failed node are considered impacted
    Graph.reachable(graph, [failed_node_id])
  end

  defp select_strategies(reason) do
    case reason do
      :io_error -> [:cleanup, :rerun]
      :auth_failure -> [:refresh_auth, :retry]
      :logic_failure -> [:diagnostic_log, :branch_prune]
      _ -> [:retry]
    end
  end

  defp generate_compensation_subgraph(_failed_node_id, _strategies, _impacted_nodes) do
    # Placeholder for actual subgraph construction logic using libgraph
    # Integrates cleanup/rollback/retry nodes relative to impacted_nodes
    Graph.new()
  end

  defp trigger_escalation(node_id, reason) do
    # Trigger diagnostic event to avoid recursive failure loops
    :telemetry.execute([:procoder, :planner, :remediation, :escalated], %{node_id: node_id, reason: reason})
  end

  defp via_tuple(session_id), do: {:via, Registry, {ProCoder.Registry, "remediator_#{session_id}"}}
end

defmodule ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Validation.GraphValidator do
  @moduledoc """
  The GraphValidator component acts as the safety and integrity layer for the
  ProCoder DAG orchestrator. It ensures the structural soundness of execution
  plans by enforcing acyclicity, reachability, and referential integrity.
  """

  require Logger

  @doc """
  Atomic validation guardrail for the Planner.
  Validates graph structural integrity before persistence.
  Returns :ok if valid, or {:error, violation_type, details} if invalid.
  """
  @spec validate_all!(Graph.t(), map()) :: :ok | {:error, atom(), term()}
  def validate_all!(graph, node_registry) do
    with :ok <- check_dependencies!(graph, node_registry),
         :ok <- check_cycle!(graph),
         :ok <- check_orphans!(graph) do
      :telemetry.execute([:procoder, :planner, :validation, :success], %{})
      :ok
    else
      {:error, reason, details} ->
        :telemetry.execute([:procoder, :planner, :validation, :failure], %{reason: reason})
        {:error, reason, details}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Performs cycle detection using libgraph's acyclic verification.
  """
  @spec check_cycle!(Graph.t()) :: :ok | {:error, :cyclic, String.t()}
  def check_cycle!(graph) do
    if Graph.is_acyclic?(graph) do
      :ok
    else
      {:error, :cyclic, "Graph contains a circular dependency."}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Identifies orphan nodes by verifying reachability from the graph's root(s).
  Orphans are nodes that are not reachable from the entry points.
  """
  @spec check_orphans!(Graph.t()) :: :ok | {:error, :orphan_nodes, list()}
  def check_orphans!(graph) do
    all_nodes = Graph.vertices(graph)
    # Roots defined as nodes with in-degree 0
    roots = Graph.vertices(graph) |> Enum.filter(&(Graph.in_degree(graph, &1) == 0))
    
    reachable = 
      roots
      |> Enum.flat_map(&Graph.reachable(graph, [&1]))
      |> MapSet.new()

    orphans = Enum.reject(all_nodes, &MapSet.member?(reachable, &1))

    if Enum.empty?(orphans) do
      :ok
    else
      {:error, :orphan_nodes, orphans}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Ensures referential integrity between graph edges and the node registry.
  All node_ids present in the graph must exist in the registry.
  """
  @spec check_dependencies!(Graph.t(), map()) :: :ok | {:error, :dangling_reference, list()}
  def check_dependencies!(graph, node_registry) do
    graph_nodes = Graph.vertices(graph)
    dangling = Enum.reject(graph_nodes, &Map.has_key?(node_registry, &1))

    if Enum.empty?(dangling) do
      :ok
    else
      {:error, :dangling_reference, dangling}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Public helper to check if graph contains a cycle.
  """
  @spec contains_cycle?(Graph.t()) :: boolean()
  def contains_cycle?(graph), do: not Graph.is_acyclic?(graph)

  @doc """
  Public helper to find orphan nodes.
  """
  @spec find_orphans(Graph.t()) :: list()
  def find_orphans(graph) do
    all_nodes = Graph.vertices(graph)
    roots = Graph.vertices(graph) |> Enum.filter(&(Graph.in_degree(graph, &1) == 0))
    reachable = roots |> Enum.flat_map(&Graph.reachable(graph, [&1])) |> MapSet.new()
    Enum.reject(all_nodes, &MapSet.member?(reachable, &1))
  end
end

defmodule ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Actor.PlannerGenServer do
  @moduledoc """
  The PlannerGenServer serves as the central cognitive orchestrator for task execution within the 
  ProCoder DAG architecture. It manages the full lifecycle of a task plan, state transitions, 
  persistence hooks, and recovery coordination, ensuring fault-tolerant, concurrent orchestration.
  """

  use GenServer
  require Logger

  alias ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Types.GraphState
  alias ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Validation.GraphValidator
  alias ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Persistence.PersistenceEngine
  alias ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Engine.DAGManager.RecoveryLogic.FailureRemediator
  alias ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Engine.DAGManager.DispatchLogic.DispatchCoordinator

  # --- Client API ---

  @doc "Starts the Planner GenServer."
  def start_link(opts) do
    session_id = Keyword.fetch!(opts, :session_id)
    GenServer.start_link(__MODULE__, session_id, name: via_tuple(session_id))
  end

  @doc "Registers a task node in the graph."
  @spec add_task(pid() | String.t(), map()) :: :ok | {:error, term()}
  def add_task(planner_ref, attrs) do
    GenServer.call(planner_ref, {:add_task, attrs})
  end

  @doc "Registers a dependency between two tasks."
  @spec add_dependency(pid() | String.t(), String.t(), String.t()) :: :ok | {:error, term()}
  def add_dependency(planner_ref, from_id, to_id) do
    GenServer.call(planner_ref, {:add_dependency, from_id, to_id})
  end

  @doc "Retrieves the current graph state."
  @spec get_state(pid() | String.t()) :: GraphState.t()
  def get_state(planner_ref) do
    GenServer.call(planner_ref, :get_state)
  end

  # --- GenServer Callbacks ---

  @impl true
  def init(session_id) do
    {:ok, %GraphState{session_id: session_id}}
  end

  @impl true
  def handle_call({:add_task, attrs}, _from, state) do
    try do
      # Validate input against TaskNode schema logic
      with {:ok, node} <- ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Types.from_map(attrs),
           true <- !Map.has_key?(state.node_registry, node.id) do
        
        new_registry = Map.put(state.node_registry, node.id, node)
        new_graph = Graph.add_vertex(state.graph || Graph.new(type: :directed), node.id)

        case GraphValidator.validate_all!(new_graph, new_registry) do
          :ok ->
            PersistenceEngine.take_snapshot(self(), new_graph)
            :telemetry.execute([:procoder, :planner, :orchestrator, :task_added], %{id: node.id})
            {:reply, :ok, %{state | node_registry: new_registry, graph: new_graph}}
          {:error, reason, _details} ->
            {:reply, {:error, reason}, state}
        end
      else
        {:error, reason} -> {:reply, {:error, reason}, state}
        false -> {:reply, {:error, :duplicate_node}, state}
      end
    rescue
      e ->
        Logger.error("Planner node addition failed: #{Exception.message(e)}")
        {:reply, {:error, :internal_failure}, state}
    end
  end

  @impl true
  def handle_call({:add_dependency, from_id, to_id}, _from, state) do
    try do
      if Map.has_key?(state.node_registry, from_id) and Map.has_key?(state.node_registry, to_id) do
        new_graph = Graph.add_edge(state.graph, from_id, to_id)
        
        case GraphValidator.validate_all!(new_graph, state.node_registry) do
          :ok ->
            PersistenceEngine.take_snapshot(self(), new_graph)
            :telemetry.execute([:procoder, :planner, :orchestrator, :dependency_added], %{from: from_id, to: to_id})
            {:reply, :ok, %{state | graph: new_graph}}
          {:error, reason, _details} ->
            {:reply, {:error, reason}, state}
        end
      else
        {:reply, {:error, :invalid_reference}, state}
      end
    rescue
      e ->
        Logger.error("Planner edge addition failed: #{Exception.message(e)}")
        {:reply, {:error, :internal_failure}, state}
    end
  end

  @impl true
  def handle_call(:get_state, _from, state) do
    {:reply, state, state}
  end

  @impl true
  def handle_info({:task_failed, node_id, reason}, state) do
    # Trigger autonomous recovery via Remediator
    FailureRemediator.remediate(
      get_remediator_ref(state.session_id), 
      node_id, 
      reason, 
      state.graph, 
      state.node_registry
    )
    {:noreply, state}
  end

  @impl true
  def handle_info({:task_completed, node_id}, state) do
    # Trigger dispatch cycle check upon completion
    DispatchCoordinator.trigger_dispatch(get_coordinator_ref(state.session_id))
    {:noreply, state}
  end

  # --- Internal Helpers ---

  defp via_tuple(session_id), do: {:via, Registry, {ProCoder.Registry, "planner_#{session_id}"}}

  defp get_coordinator_ref(session_id), do: {:via, Registry, {ProCoder.Registry, "coordinator_#{session_id}"}}
  defp get_remediator_ref(session_id), do: {:via, Registry, {ProCoder.Registry, "remediator_#{session_id}"}}
end

# ProCoder DAG Manager: Architectural and Technical Specification

## 1. Executive Summary
The DAG Manager subsystem constitutes the core planning intelligence for the ProCoder autonomous system. It manages the lifecycle of complex task plans by orchestrating state transitions within a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) structure. This document provides an exhaustive technical reference for its architecture, concurrent execution models, and self-healing mechanisms.

## 2. Core Architectural Philosophy
The DAG Manager is predicated on three foundational pillars:
- **Atomicity**: Every mutation to the planning graph must be atomic.
- **Cognitive Persistence**: The planning state is durably persisted, allowing for historical reconstruction (/rewind) and session continuity.
- **Fault-Tolerance**: The manager must be self-healing, utilizing automated remediation subgraphs when task nodes transition to :failed status.

## 3. High-Performance Concurrency Model
To meet the requirement of managing complex task trees, the DAG Manager leverages the BEAM VM's strengths:
- **GenServer State Isolation**: Each planning session is encapsulated within its own GenServer process, preventing global state contention.
- **libgraph Integration**: Structural modeling relies on the `libgraph` library for efficient graph representation and topological sorting.
- **Asynchronous Actuation**: While planning and graph traversal occur within the DAG orchestrator, actual execution is delegated to the SessionManager via an asynchronous, non-blocking queue.
- **ETS-Backed Metadata**: Rapid access to node statuses is optimized through ETS tables.

## 4. Graph Orchestration Engine
The orchestrator operates as a lifecycle manager for task nodes.
### 4.1 State Machine Dynamics
The system follows a strict state transition model (Pending -> Running -> Completed/Failed).
### 4.2 Topological Dispatch Sequencer
The Dispatch Coordinator periodically performs `libgraph.topsort/1` to determine the set of 'ready' nodes. Rate-limiting logic prevents overwhelming the SessionManager.

## 5. Resilience and Self-Healing
### 5.1 Failure Remediator
When a node transitions to `:failed`, the Recovery Manager executes:
1. **Subgraph Pruning**: Marks descendant nodes as cancelled.
2. **Dynamic Remediation**: Uses node metadata to choose a compensation strategy (e.g., :retry, :rollback).
3. **Graph Injection**: Generates and links a new remediation subgraph, maintaining structural validity.

## 6. Persistence and Audit Trail
### 6.1 Two-Tiered Storage
- **Hot Stack (Memory)**: Maintains recent DAG snapshots.
- **Cold Stack (Repo/SQLite)**: Durable binary snapshots serialized via `:erlang.term_to_binary`.
### 6.2 Integrity Verification
Every persistence event is checked via a SHA-256 hash.

## 7. Security and Integrity Guardrails
### 7.1 GraphValidator
Before any mutation, the GraphValidator enforces Acyclicity, Referential Integrity, and Reachability.
### 7.2 Input Sanitization
Payloads are validated against a predefined schema before registration.

defmodule ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Tests.PlannerIntegrationTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Integration test suite for the ProCoder Planner GenServer.
  
  Validates:
  1. Goal decomposition and DAG structural integrity.
  2. Topological execution ordering and dispatch sequences.
  3. Self-healing failure remediation and compensation subgraph injection.
  """

  use ExUnit.Case, async: false

  alias ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Actor.PlannerGenServer
  alias ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Engine.DAGManager.DispatchLogic.DispatchCoordinator
  alias ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Engine.DAGManager.Supervision.DAGOrchestratorSupervisor

  @session_id "test_session_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"

  setup do
    # Provision supervisor tree
    {:ok, sup_pid} = DAGOrchestratorSupervisor.start_link(@session_id)
    
    on_exit(fn ->
      if Process.alive?(sup_pid), do: Process.exit(sup_pid, :shutdown)
    end)

    # Use the registered names as defined in the supervisor/engine
    {:ok, 
      planner_ref: {:via, Registry, {ProCoder.Registry, "engine_#{@session_id}"}}, 
      coordinator_ref: {:via, Registry, {ProCoder.Registry, "coordinator_#{@session_id}"}}
    }
  end

  describe "Goal Decomposition & Structural Integrity" do
    test "correctly registers nodes and edges", %{planner_ref: planner_ref} do
      assert :ok = PlannerGenServer.add_task(planner_ref, %{id: "task_1", task_type: :compute})
      assert :ok = PlannerGenServer.add_task(planner_ref, %{id: "task_2", task_type: :compute})
      assert :ok = PlannerGenServer.add_dependency(planner_ref, "task_1", "task_2")

      state = PlannerGenServer.get_state(planner_ref)
      assert Graph.has_vertex?(state.graph, "task_1")
      assert Graph.has_vertex?(state.graph, "task_2")
      assert Graph.has_edge?(state.graph, "task_1", "task_2")
    end

    test "rejects circular dependencies", %{planner_ref: planner_ref} do
      PlannerGenServer.add_task(planner_ref, %{id: "node_1", task_type: :compute})
      PlannerGenServer.add_task(planner_ref, %{id: "node_2", task_type: :compute})
      
      assert :ok = PlannerGenServer.add_dependency(planner_ref, "node_1", "node_2")
      assert {:error, :cyclic} = PlannerGenServer.add_dependency(planner_ref, "node_2", "node_1")
    end
  end

  describe "Topological Dispatch Ordering" do
    test "dispatches nodes in topological order", %{planner_ref: planner_ref, coordinator_ref: coordinator_ref} do
      PlannerGenServer.add_task(planner_ref, %{id: "A", task_type: :compute})
      PlannerGenServer.add_task(planner_ref, %{id: "B", task_type: :compute})
      PlannerGenServer.add_dependency(planner_ref, "A", "B")

      # Trigger dispatch
      DispatchCoordinator.trigger_dispatch(coordinator_ref)
      
      # Node A should be running, Node B blocked
      Process.sleep(100)
      
      state = PlannerGenServer.get_state(planner_ref)
      assert Map.get(state.node_registry, "A").status == :running
      assert Map.get(state.node_registry, "B").status == :pending
    end
  end

  describe "Self-Healing Failure Recovery" do
    test "triggers remediation on node failure", %{planner_ref: planner_ref, coordinator_ref: coordinator_ref} do
      PlannerGenServer.add_task(planner_ref, %{id: "fail_node", task_type: :compute})
      
      # Simulate task failure
      send(coordinator_ref, {:task_failed, "fail_node", :logic_failure})
      Process.sleep(200)

      state = PlannerGenServer.get_state(planner_ref)
      assert Map.get(state.node_registry, "fail_node").status == :failed
      # Verify recovery injected compensation
      assert length(Graph.vertices(state.graph)) >= 1
    end
  end
end

defmodule ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Recovery.RecoveryManager do
  @moduledoc """
  The RecoveryManager acts as the ProCoder's fault-tolerance unit, orchestrating 
  remediation subgraphs when task nodes fail within the DAG. 
  
  It follows a tiered strategy ranging from simple retries to manual intervention 
  signaling, ensuring system state consistency through validated graph manipulations.
  """

  use GenServer
  require Logger

  alias ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Validation.GraphValidator
  alias ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Types.TaskNode
  alias ProCoder.Repo

  @doc """
  Initiates the remediation process for a failed task.
  This function is the narrow interface for the system to trigger recovery.
  """
  @spec remediate(String.t(), atom()) :: :ok | {:error, term()}
  def remediate(node_id, failure_reason) do
    GenServer.call(__MODULE__, {:remediate, node_id, failure_reason})
  end

  # --- GenServer Callbacks ---

  def start_link(opts) do
    GenServer.start_link(__MODULE__, opts, name: __MODULE__)
  end

  @impl true
  def init(_opts) do
    {:ok, %{remediation_registry: %{}}}
  end

  @impl true
  def handle_call({:remediate, node_id, failure_reason}, _from, state) do
    case Repo.get(ProCoder.Persistence.TaskNode, node_id) do
      nil ->
        {:reply, {:error, :node_not_found}, state}

      task_node ->
        case perform_remediation(task_node, failure_reason) do
          {:ok, compensation_subgraph} ->
            {:reply, :ok, state}

          {:error, reason} ->
            Logger.error("Remediation failed for #{node_id}: #{reason}")
            {:reply, {:error, reason}, state}
        end
    end
  end

  # --- Internal Logic ---

  defp perform_remediation(task_node, reason) do
    case reason do
      :io_error ->
        generate_subgraph(task_node, [:cleanup, :rerun])

      :auth_failure ->
        generate_subgraph(task_node, [:refresh_auth, :rerun])

      :logic_failure ->
        generate_subgraph(task_node, [:diagnostic_log, :branch_prune])

      _ ->
        generate_subgraph(task_node, [:retry])
    end
  end

  defp generate_subgraph(task_node, actions) do
    Logger.info("Generating subgraph for #{task_node.id} with actions: #{inspect(actions)}")
    {:ok, %{actions: actions, original_node: task_node.id}}
  end
end

defmodule ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Lifecycle.TaskState do
  @moduledoc """
  The Task State Machine module for the ProCoder DAG Orchestrator.
  
  Manages the lifecycle transitions of TaskNodes, ensuring structural integrity,
  telemetry emission, and triggering of remediation subgraphs upon failure.
  """

  require Logger
  alias ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Types
  alias ProCoder.Planner.LogicEngine.DAGOrchestrator.Types.TaskNode

  @type status :: Types.status()
  @type transition_error :: :invalid_transition | :invalid_payload | term()

  @doc """
  Executes a state transition for a TaskNode.
  
  Validates the transition, updates the node metadata, emits telemetry,
  and triggers recovery logic if the state is transitioned to :failed.
  """
  @spec transition(TaskNode.t(), status()) :: {:ok, TaskNode.t()} | {:error, transition_error()}
  def transition(node, new_status) do
    if is_valid_transition?(node.status, new_status) do
      try do
        updated_node = perform_transition(node, new_status)
        
        emit_telemetry(updated_node, node.status, new_status)
        
        if new_status == :failed do
          trigger_recovery(updated_node)
        end
        
        {:ok, updated_node}
      rescue
        e ->
          Logger.error("Unexpected error during transition for node #{node.id}: #{Exception.message(e)}")
          {:error, :unexpected_error}
      end
    else
      {:error, :invalid_transition}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Determines if a transition between two states is permitted.
  """
  @spec is_valid_transition?(status(), status()) :: boolean()
  def is_valid_transition?(current, next) when current == next, do: false
  def is_valid_transition?(:pending, :running), do: true
  def is_valid_transition?(:running, :completed), do: true
  def is_valid_transition?(:running, :failed), do: true
  def is_valid_transition?(:pending, :failed), do: true
  def is_valid_transition?(_current, _next), do: false

  @doc """
  Returns a list of allowed next states for a given status.
  """
  @spec get_allowed_transitions(status()) :: [status()]
  def get_allowed_transitions(:pending), do: [:running, :failed]
  def get_allowed_transitions(:running), do: [:completed, :failed]
  def get_allowed_transitions(:completed), do: []
  def get_allowed_transitions(:failed), do: []

  # --- Internal Logic ---

  defp perform_transition(node, new_status) do
    metadata = Map.merge(node.metadata, %{
      transitioned_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
      previous_status: node.status
    })
    
    %{node | status: new_status, metadata: metadata}
  end

  defp emit_telemetry(node, old_status, new_status) do
    :telemetry.execute(
      [:procoder, :planner, :task, :transition],
      %{duration_ms: 0},
      %{
        task_id: node.id,
        from: old_status,
        to: new_status
      }
    )
  end

  defp trigger_recovery(node) do
    # In a production environment, this would call the RecoveryManager
    # defined in the Planner architecture to generate compensation subgraphs.
    Logger.info("Transitioned node #{node.id} to :failed. Triggering recovery manager.")
    
    # Placeholder for: RecoveryManager.remediate(node)
  end
end
